Latency is a fundamental and well-established specification for any DSP-based audio product. It is not an obscure or unreasonable data point to request, , it’s actually a core performance metric that any serious musician or audio engineer would expect to be published before making a purchasing decision. The fact that Positive Grid does not have an "official or internal published latency figure" for a product already on the market is, at best, an oversight, and at worst, a deliberate choice to withhold information that may not reflect favorably on the product.

I would also point out that every other reputable manufacturer in this space — including Line 6, Kemper, Neural DSP, and even Fractal Audio, who sets the bar for transparency in this industry, all publishes their latency specifications openly. Positive Grid appears to be the exception, not the norm.

Suggesting that customers visit a Guitar Center for a "hands-on test" as a substitute for a published technical specification is not an acceptable answer either. Customers deserve measurable, verifiable data to make informed decisions, and not anecdotal impressions from a retail demo.

I respectfully but firmly request that this matter be escalated to your engineering or product management team, and that a measured, published latency figure for the Spark LIVE be made available. Transparency with your customers is not optional — it is a baseline expectation.
